fact: The UNDP/Neuralio feasibility study says METEO RWANDA receives satellite data from EUMETSAT's Meteosat Second and Third Generation via EUMETCast, with imagery as often as every 15 minutes, used mainly as static images (JPEG cloud maps) by forecasters.

The FMI peer review says Rwanda accesses EUMETSAT satellite products through a ground-based satellite receiver, and that Meteo Rwanda's forecasting draws on EUMETSAT satellite imagery alongside a C-band radar.
The FMI peer review says Meteo Rwanda has an ISO9001:2015 certified QMS since 2018, last audited in 2022 and valid until 2025, including all branches of service.
system: Meteo Rwanda ISO 9001:2015 quality management system

fact: Meteo Rwanda's deck says it runs PUMA-2025 reception stations giving real-time processing and visualisation of MTG satellite data alongside its radar network.

Meteo Rwanda says its severe thunderstorm warning lead time rose from 15 minutes in 2021 to a projected 60 minutes in 2026, with a significant jump since MTG start, and describes impact-based flash flood and storm warnings.
Meteo Rwanda's deck states its operations are ISO 9001:2015 certified.
The African Union Commission's ClimSA deck lists Rwanda among 41 of 49 member states with a PUMA station installed as at 12 May 2026; the station carries satellite imagery.
